headline: Do not promise a reply time you cannot keep
subtext: Recipients and staff can update the Waiting status text with a realistic timeframe and tell sources where to check for an update.
image_alt_text: Light-mode Hush Line social graphic titled “Do not promise a reply time you cannot keep.” Beside it, the desktop Message Statuses screen shows Waiting, a Status Text field promising a reply in 24–72 hours, and the Update Reply Text button. The graphic presents reviewing that promise as the safer workflow for recipients and staff.

social.bluesky: Mistake to avoid: leaving an old reply-time promise in place. Hush Line recipients and staff can edit the Waiting status text shown on a source’s temporary page. Use a timeframe your team can meet, then check the wording before sharing the tip line.
social.linkedin:
A common intake mistake is leaving a reply-time promise in place after staffing or schedules change.

Hush Line’s Message Statuses settings let recipients and staff edit the Waiting status text shown on the temporary page a source can check after sending a message. Give a timeframe your team can meet, and tell the source to return to that page for an update.

Before you share a tip line, compare the Waiting message with how your team actually handles replies.
social.mastodon:
An outdated Waiting message can promise sources a reply time your team cannot meet.

In Hush Line’s Message Statuses settings, recipients and staff can edit the text shown on the temporary page a source can check after sending a message. Use an honest timeframe and remind the source to return for updates.

Before sharing the tip line, read the Waiting message against your current reply process.

rationale: All three candidates are cooldown fallbacks. Message Statuses is the least recently used topic in the shortlist, and this angle is distinct from prior posts about plain wording or simply explaining the Waiting page. It identifies a concrete operational mistake—an outdated reply-time promise—and gives recipients and staff a direct check they can repeat before sharing a tip line.
copy_brief: Write for recipients and staff using Hush Line day to day, not for platform admins.
